items.text: In the preparation and purification of any organic compound, there are likely tobe several techniques used.Eachpreparation or synthesiswill useone ormore ofthetechniquesinthis section and the next. Most of them have been covered in Book 1, but all are included inthesesectionsforcompleteness.

items.text: Some reactions involving organic compounds are slow at room temperature,so the obvious thing to dois heat thereactionmixture. However as many organic compounds are volatile, there is a risk that they will escape from the reaction mixture during the heating process. The normal way to prevent this happening is to heat the reaction mixture in a flask fitted with a reflux condenser (fig A). This technique is alsokmown asrefuxing.All thevapoursrisingfromthe reaction mixture during heating enter the condenser and change back into liquids. items.label: text
items.text: The advantages of using simple distillation, rather than fractional distillation, are that it is easier to set up and is quicker The disadvantage is that it does not separate the liquids as well as fractional distillation. It should only be used if the boiling temperature of the liquid being purified is very different from the otherliquids in themixture,ideally a difference ofmore than25°C.
